purpose: What a document says students may or may not use AI for, in which setting, and what must be acknowledged. One row per document per use and setting, plus document-level rules, each with a verbatim quote. Anything not stated stays empty.

uses.label: Plan or structure work
uses.definition: Outlines, essay plans, structuring an argument or report.

uses.label: Explain concepts or act as a tutor
uses.definition: Explaining concepts, answering questions, acting as a study buddy or personal tutor.

uses.label: Summarise or explain sources
uses.definition: Summarising or explaining readings, papers or documents the student supplies.

uses.label: Find literature or sources
uses.definition: Literature searching, suggesting sources or references.

uses.label: Revise or practise
uses.definition: Revision aids, practice questions, quizzes, flashcards, study plans.

uses.label: Get feedback on a draft
uses.definition: Asking for feedback or suggestions on the student's own draft without the AI rewriting it.

uses.label: Check spelling and grammar
uses.definition: Spelling, grammar, punctuation, proofreading and basic language editing.

uses.label: Translate
uses.definition: Translating text, including as a language-learning aid.

uses.label: Rewrite or paraphrase own text
uses.definition: Rewording, restyling or improving the student's own text beyond proofreading.

uses.label: Generate assessed text
uses.definition: Having AI write, answer or complete part or all of an assessed piece of work.

uses.label: Include AI output in submitted work
uses.definition: Quoting, adapting or including AI-generated text, images or other output in what is submitted, usually with attribution.

uses.label: Analyse data
uses.definition: Data analysis, statistics, charts or visualisation.

uses.label: Create images, audio or video
uses.definition: Producing images, audio, video, slides or other media.

uses.label: Format references
uses.definition: Formatting reference lists or citations with AI.

uses.label: Record, transcribe or summarise meetings
uses.definition: AI recording, live transcription, meeting or lecture notes.

uses.label: Assistive use
uses.definition: AI as assistive technology or an agreed adjustment for disabled students or students with additional needs.

uses.label: Rely on AI as a source of facts
uses.definition: Treating AI output as a reliable source, or citing AI as an authority, instead of checking primary sources.

contexts.study: learning and preparation that is not itself assessed
contexts.assessed_work: coursework or any work submitted for assessment
contexts.research_or_thesis: a dissertation, thesis or research project

stances.conditional: allowed only if a condition holds (set in conditions)
stances.discouraged: advised against, or a caution, but not forbidden
stances.required: the assessment or course requires this use

conditions.needs_permission: only if the module, lecturer, brief or tutor allows it
conditions.needs_acknowledgement: only if the use is acknowledged or declared
conditions.approved_tool_only: only with an institution-approved or provided tool
conditions.limited_extent: only up to a stated extent (a share of the work, minor changes, not substantive)
conditions.no_personal_data: only without personal or confidential data
conditions.other_rules_apply: only subject to other rules (placement, client, publisher, ethics)
conditions.account_or_age_limit: only within a stated account or age limit
conditions.not_required_to_use: students are not required to use AI for this

acknowledge.required: the document says this use must be acknowledged or declared
acknowledge.not_required: the document says this use needs no acknowledgement

default_when_silent.prohibit_all: when the brief says nothing, no AI use is allowed
default_when_silent.permit_all: when the brief says nothing, AI use is allowed
default_when_silent.permit_with_acknowledgement: when the brief says nothing, AI use is allowed if acknowledged
default_when_silent.ask_instructor: when the brief says nothing, ask the lecturer or tutor
default_when_silent.use_by_use_rule: when the brief says nothing, per-use rules apply
default_when_silent.differs_by_assessment_type: when the brief says nothing, the default depends on the type of assessment
default_when_silent.treated_as_human_assistance: AI help is treated like help from another person
default_when_silent.misconduct_only_if_unacknowledged: use is misconduct only if not acknowledged

decided_by.institution_wide: one rule for the whole institution
decided_by.school_or_department: set by school, faculty or department
decided_by.module_or_lecturer: set by the module leader or lecturer
decided_by.tiered_scale: set by a named scale or categories of permitted use

duty.conditional: acknowledgement depends on a condition (extent, a course rule, assessment type)

records.required: students must keep records (chats, drafts, notes)

referencing.cite_in_reference_list: AI output must be cited with a reference list entry
referencing.acknowledge_without_reference_entry: acknowledge in the text or a statement, no reference list entry
referencing.follow_guide: follow the library or institution referencing guide
referencing.not_required_in_reference_list: no reference list entry is needed

consequence.submission_blocked: the work cannot be submitted without it
consequence.treated_as_misconduct: missing acknowledgement is treated as misconduct
consequence.safe_if_declared: properly declared permitted use is not misconduct
